title: Echinacea infusion for cold prevention
subtitle: A short-course tea of Echinacea purpurea herb for immune support at the first sign of a cold
excerpt: Echinacea infusion is a hot tea of dried Echinacea purpurea aerial parts steeped for 10 minutes, taken at the first sign of a cold for 5 to 7 days. The immunomodulatory polysaccharides and alkylamides in echinacea are best extracted by hot-water infusion of the aerial parts. Not for long-term continuous use. One to three cups a day for a short course.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), echinacea entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Echinacea purpurea (L.) Moench, herba (2015, EMA/HMPC/557979/2013), open access. Cochrane review: Karsch-Völk M et al., Echinacea for preventing and treating the common cold (2015).

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb or preparation that modifies the activity of the immune system, stimulating a sluggish response when fighting infection, or dampening an overactive response in allergy or autoimmune conditions. Echinacea is classified as an immunostimulant for short-course use.

, taken for 5 to 7 days to support the immune response. A mild tongue tingle is normal. Some trials found it shortened cold duration. The infusion is mild, earthy, and aromatic.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: dried Echinacea purpurea aerial parts (herb and flower)

content.text: Place 2 teaspoons of dried echinacea aerial parts in a teapot or heatproof cup. Pour 200 ml of just-boiled water over the herb. Cover and steep for 10 minutes.
Strain into a cup and drink warm. A slight tingling or numbness on the tongue and lips is normal, this is caused by the alkylamides and indicates a good-quality herb.
Three cups daily for the first two days of a cold, then two cups daily for the remaining 3 to 5 days. Maximum 7 to 10 days per course. Allow at least 2 weeks before repeating.
Dried echinacea aerial parts store 12 months in a sealed tin away from light and heat. Brew each cup fresh.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use if you have an Asteraceae allergy, an autoimmune condition, or take immunosuppressant drugs. See a doctor if symptoms worsen after 5 days or do not improve by 10 days. Seek medical care for high fever, chest pain, or difficulty breathing.
